heading: Why this is not a feature flag but a capability opt-in
text:
### Why this is not a feature flag but a capability opt-in [LDTL.1.3]

The performance difference is real and significant.  For N_max = 100,000
facts and expired = 1,000 per tick:

| Mode | Tick cost | Formula |
|---|---|---|
| Default (per-schema FIFO queue) | O(expired × log n_schemas + n_schemas) | n_schemas ≈ 10–50; ≈ 1,000 × 6 = 6,000 at 50 |
| `dynamic_ttl` (deadline heap) | O(expired × log N_ttl) | ≈ 1,000 × 17 = 17,000 |

The default removes N_ttl from the tick cost: its one log factor is in the
number of TTL schemas, a compile-time constant ([LDTL.6.1]).  A
program that never uses per-emit TTL override pays no cost for the
capability.
